newsitem.title: CHINA: Influx of Vietnamese boatpeople worries HK's Tung.
newsitem.headline: Influx of Vietnamese boatpeople worries HK's Tung.

text.p: Hong Kong chief executive Tung Chee-hwa said on Thursday he was concerned about the recent influx of Vietnamese boatpeople into the territory and that his government would soon decide how to solve the problem.

His comments come just hours after the government repatriated a group of 102 Vietnamese migrants, the first batch to be sent back after this former British colony returned to Chinese rule five weeks ago.
The returnees, commonly called boatpeople because many arrive by sea, included 97 men and five women. They had been held in a closed camp since arriving here last year, a government statement said.
The repatriation follows the capture of some two dozen new Vietnamese boatpeople earlier this week after police carried out a massive land, sea and air search across an outlying island.

"We all note with concern the recent influx of refugees. And we are taking a very serious look at the whole issue and we hope to be in a position to tell you what we intend to do in the very near future," Tung told reporters.
Prominent local figures have urged the scrapping of Hong Kong's "first port of asylum status", a legacy of British rule which finds little favour with the territory's 6.4 million population.
The boatpeople drama began when tens of thousands of Vietnamese fled the country after the 1975 Communist victory in the Vietnam War.
Some 3,000 boatpeople are still held in detention in Hong Kong despite China's repeated calls to Britain to clear the camps before Beijing took over on July 1.
However, Beijing appears now to be leaving it to Hong Kong, which is guaranteed a high degree of autonomy under its post-handover constitution, to continue the repatriation programme as best it can.
Security sources were quoted by newspapers on Thursday as saying the new Hong Kong government was lobbying Hanoi to speed up the process.
